newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian leftist leader discusses EMU with Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Italian leftist leader discusses EMU with Kohl.

text.p: Massimo D'Alema, leader of the main party in Italy's ruling coalition, said his meeting on Thursday with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was "positive and reassuring" on the subject of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The ex-communist Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) said in a statement that D'Alema had met Kohl in Bonn on Thursday morning in a meeting which had been scheduled for several weeks.

"Regarding the newspaper reports relating to the process of European monetary union which are currently occupying Italian public opinion, the talk with the Chancellor was positive and reassuring," the statement said.
On Wednesday the Financial Times daily newspaper reported that a plan was being prepared to get Italy to delay its entry into a single European currency at its projected 1999 start.
The existence of such a plan was denied by Bonn, Brussels and Rome with Prime Minister Romano Prodi reiterating Italy's determination to meet tough EMU criteria.

Prodi, who is due to meet Kohl in Bonn on Friday, told Italian newspapers published on Thursday he would use the trip to tell Kohl that constant reports doubting Italy's fitness for EMU were unhelpful to the common cause of building monetary union.
Recently, German business executives and a top economic advisor to Kohl have cast doubt over Italy's ability to meet the stiff criteria in time for the EMU deadline.

Italy wants to be in at the start of the single currency and Prodi said he would tell Kohl that the government proposed bringing forward its 1998 budget to try to banish doubts about Italy's determination to respect the Maastricht criteria.
